blindSummary:
This state/province recorded zero transgender killings in 2024 but jumped to 4 in 2025 - the sharpest deterioration in the national monitoring dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yields approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate of any state in the country in 2025 and roughly three times the national rate of ~0.38 per million. The monitoring report cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

This rate-driven exposure places the state/province modestly below the country-wide baseline. Compared with a peer state/province in the same regional bloc whose 2025 count was 8, this state's absolute count is lower (4 vs 8) but its per-capita risk is actually higher; the deviation from the national baseline is therefore slightly larger than the raw numbers might suggest. The state sits within the bloc of states that together accounted for 38 of the 80 national killings in 2025.

No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal. For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly.
